review_text: This film blew me away from the opening scene. The direction is bold, the acting is heartfelt, and the score stayed with me for days.
A little slow in the second act but the payoff in the final twenty minutes is completely earned.
I wanted to like this so much more than I did. The pacing drags in the middle act and the ending feels rushed.
A solid, workmanlike thriller. Nothing groundbreaking, but it does exactly what it sets out to do.
The financial jargon is dense but the family drama underneath more than makes up for it.
Absolutely dreadful. The dialogue is wooden, the plot makes no sense, and I checked my phone more than the screen.
Loud, forgettable, and clearly missing the crew that made the first one work.
One of the most emotionally honest coming-of-age... wait, sisterhood stories I've seen in years. The lead performance is a revelation.
The visuals are stunning but the story is paper-thin. Style over substance, unfortunately.
Gorgeous world-building. I would happily watch two more hours of just the ship's corridors.
A charming little indie gem. Low budget, huge heart. I laughed and cried in equal measure.
The sequel completely squanders the goodwill of the original. Lazy writing, worse jokes.
Genuinely tense practical stunt work. They don't make chase movies like this anymore.
Competent but forgettable. I'd already stopped thinking about it by the time I got home.
Every frame is a painting. This director has outdone themselves, a masterclass in tension.
The mining-station politics are surprisingly gripping. Best sci-fi of the year for me.
The lead actor is miscast and it drags the whole film down with him.
A cozy, predictable rom-com that hits every beat you expect, and that's exactly why it works.
Convoluted plot twists that exist purely to confuse, not to reward attentive viewers.
Genuinely terrifying. I haven't slept properly since watching this at midnight.
A haunted-house movie with actual heart. The final act made me tear up, unexpectedly.
The soundtrack alone is worth the price of admission. Everything else is just a bonus.
Painfully slow first hour that the rushed finale can't make up for.
A quiet, patient drama that trusts its audience. Refreshing in an era of noise.
The CGI looks like it belongs in a video game from a decade ago. Distracting throughout.
Funny, sharp, and surprisingly tender by the end. A great date-night pick.
I respect the ambition, but the film collapses under the weight of its own ideas.
Every jump scare is telegraphed a mile away. Genuinely more funny than frightening.
A career-best performance anchors an otherwise uneven script.
Whip-smart dialogue and a cast that clearly loves being there. Pure fun.
An eye-opening look at a subject I thought I already understood. Essential viewing.
Style-heavy but scare-light — no wait, this one actually delivers. Genuinely unnerving concept.
The found-footage-via-filter gimmick shouldn't work this well. Scared me off social media for a week.
Twisty in a good way, the kind of thriller you immediately want to rewatch.
A tender, unhurried farewell to a way of life. One of the best dramas of the decade so far.
Inventive, colorful, and surprisingly moving for a movie about a glitching video game character.
Gorgeous fantasy worldbuilding with a genuinely clever central idea about maps and memory.
A sweet, low-key romance that earns its slow burn. Perfect one-sitting watch.
The meteor-shower motif is used so well. One of my favorite endings this year.
Dense mythology but the emotional core (a daughter finishing her father's work) never gets lost.
